answer: Network-coordinate uniqueness resists sybils. Each key locks a slashable bond and must answer randomized pings from a ring of public beacons. Replies form one signed measurement thread that has to arrive before a short time horizon. If two keys' delay profiles wander into the same locus, or a ping is missed, every linked deposit is slashed. Clones on one host cannot occupy many vantage points at once, so a farm needs distinct network locations and distinct bonds for every identity; attacker cost scales with real presence and capital, not with free keypairs.
